It is almost axionatic that when natural areas are subdivided for residential use, the amount of paving from streets, driveways, parking lots, roof tops, etc., almost always increases peak runoff and contributes to the detrimental effect of increasing peak flood flows influencing areas downstream. On only one project is this phenomena recognized and plans to mitigate it included. Two projects have lakes involved and in these cases particular attention is being given to prevent contamination of the lakes by sediment and other pollutants. Unless the same care is taken on the other projects similar damage will be done to other water bodies downstream whether these be lakes, streams, rivers, estuaries, beaches, etc. The sediment and other litter washed off from the new subdivision must end up in somebody's body of water unless it is stopped at the source. On one site, it is proposed to recharge storm runoff into the ground water in lieu of allowing it to flow into a lake. No mention is made about how the water will be handled to prevent contamination of the ground water.
Unless the interdisciplinary team planning these projects has on it an experienced soil and water conservationist who knows now to plan both the use and treatment of land, these projects show great potential for repeating the mistakes of the past.
The proposal appears to ' ly partially relevant to rural housing needs. The emphasis appears to be on planning systems and designs for urban areas.
Rural homes and subdivisions may eventually profit by the advances made in good site planning and new techniques of sewage disposal, water supply and climate control proven through Breakthrough.
On page 4, the statement describes a departure from use of conventional materials, "Where upwards of 75 percent of residential building in the United States uses wood as its basic structural material, this proportion is nearly exactly reversed among the 22 selected systems in Operation Breakthmouth. Roughly one-fourth of the syst mouse a wood structure while the remaining three-fourths use concrete, metal or plastic structures. This is especially important as a means of encouraging competition in the market place among the alternative materials." Long-term maintenance and repair programs are essential for any housing complex if environmental quality is to be maintained. It is, therefore, suggested proposals include specific details on how such long-term care will be accomplished and financed. The statement should make an evaluation of the environmental impact of this proposed departure, including relative pollution problems associated with development, utilization, and manufacture of various building materials.
